ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, directors, and authorized representatives against: (i) the consolidated list issued by the State Bank of Viet Nam; (ii) UN Security Council consolidated sanctions list; (iii) OFAC sanctions/OFAC SDN lists; (iv) EU financial sanctions lists; (v) FATF high-risk jurisdictions; and (vi) domestic Vietnamese PEP list. Enhanced due diligence mandatory for PEPs, high-risk jurisdictions, and politically exposed persons; adverse media screening and negative news checks are required as part of standard AML/CFT compliance.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: National Business Registration Portal (Cổng thông tin quốc gia về đăng ký doanh nghiệp) - https://dangkykinhdoanh.gov.vn
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Vietnamese company names must be rendered in the Vietnamese alphabet (including diacritics where applicable). The legal name must consist of a type designation ('Công ty TNHH' for LLC) and a proper name. Foreign-invested companies may also register an additional foreign-language name, provided the Vietnamese name is distinct. Transliteration must be consistent with Vietnamese pronunciation and spelling rules; names of foreign origin must not conflict with existing registered names or violate cultural/normative standards.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Names identical or confusingly similar to an existing registered enterprise
Names using state-enterprise, government agency, or military terminology without authorization
Names contrary to historical, cultural, national, or ethical values
Words such as 'Bank', 'Insurance', 'Securities', 'Audit', 'Law Firm', 'Military', 'Government' or equivalent protected/sensitive terms without prior ministerial approval
Names involving administrative units (e.g., 'Bộ', 'Sở', 'UBND') unless permission granted
Words denoting political organizations or socio-political organizations without consent
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: In the event of a name rejection, the applicant may file a written administrative appeal with the Director of the Provincial Department of Planning and Investment (DPI) within 30 days of receiving the rejection notice. The appeal must state grounds for contesting the rejection and include any supporting documents. Alternatively, the applicant may submit a revised name for re-examination through the National Business Registration Portal. If the appeal is dismissed, recourse may be available through administrative court proceedings under Vietnamese law. Names automatically expire after 30 days if not fully incorporated within the window.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Virtual offices are generally not permissible as the sole registered address for a Vietnamese LLC. A physical registered address in Viet Nam is required. However, serviced offices or co-working spaces that provide a physical address and reception services may be acceptable if they meet the statutory requirement of a lawful physical premises for the registered office. For a remote BPO call center, a physical registered office must be maintained for service of process and regulatory contact.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High (75%+ likelihood for newly incorporated LLCs, particularly foreign-invested entities in the BPO/outsourcing industry; local authorities may conduct unannounced inspections to verify physical presence and compliance with Article 42 of Enterprise Law 2020)

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: General Department of Taxation (GDT), Ministry of Finance, Socialist Republic of Vietnam; official electronic tax portal: etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn (enterprise self-service e-filing and registration).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign-invested LLC registers for taxation with the Provincial/City Tax Department where the head office is located by submitting the Tax Registration Form (Form 01-ĐK-TCT), Article of Incorporation, investment certificate (IRC/ERC), and legal representative identification. The tax authority issues a single Tax Identification Number (Mã số thuế, MST) that functions as the TIN, VAT identification number, and customs identification number, typically within 15 working days from valid submission. Tax registration is automatically integrated with the National Business Registration System under the One-Stop Shop mechanism.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; a Vietnamese resident enterprise (foreign-invested LLC) is taxed on worldwide income at 20% CIT; no pass-through or partner-level taxation is available.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Vietnam does not operate U.S.-style check-the-box or hybrid mismatch elections. The LLC is irrevocably classified as a resident corporate taxpayer. Only limited routine elections exist, such as choosing the accounting period (calendar year or other fiscal year subject to tax authority approval), and selecting between the regular VAT credit method and the direct tax computation method for foreign contractor contexts, but for an ordinary local LLC, VAT is mandatory under the credit method once taxable revenue exceeds the registration threshold.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No VAT registration turnover threshold applies to companies formed under the Enterprise Law; every foreign-invested LLC must register for VAT immediately. For household and individual businesses the conservative threshold is VND 100,000,000 annual revenue; an LLC with BPO services is always mandatorily registered regardless of revenue level.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory electronic invoicing under Decree 123/2020/ND-CP and Circular 78/2021/TT-BTC. All invoices must be generated in the national e-invoice portal format and, for invoices issued using the tax-authority-code method, are subject to pre-validation and assignment of a digital tax authority code before issuance. Real-time machine-readable XML (standardized by GDT) and API integration with the e-invoice gateway are compulsory for certified invoicing applications. No physical invoice stamping is required.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export zero-rating applies to goods physically exported from Vietnam and to services supplied to and consumed by a foreign customer outside Vietnam, including offshore BPO/call-center services, provided that the service is not consumed or used in Vietnam. The exporter must possess a written contract with the foreign party, documentary evidence of actual service performance, and verified non-cash payment from abroad through a Vietnamese licensed bank or through foreign banks and international payment intermediaries (e.g., Wise B2B, SWIFT wire) with conclusive bank statements. The VAT rate is 0%; input VAT attributable to export activities is refundable under VAT credit method.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (both e-declaration and confirmed customs clearance) for physical goods
Commercial Invoice / Service Invoice evidencing BPO service scope, customer identity, and transaction price
Signed BPO services agreement (in English or Vietnamese) with clear offshore deliverable clauses
Bill of Lading / Airway Bill (only when tangible goods are involved; not applicable to pure call-center services)
Inward Remittance Certificate (IRC) or equivalent bank remittance advice evidencing non-cash payment from the overseas counterparty
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Zero-rating claims are audited against export contracts, customs declarations, service performance records, and inbound remittance evidence. False export declarations or fraudulent zero-rating claims attract VAT reassessment plus tax evasion penalties under Circular 166/2013/TT-BTC and criminal liability under Penal Code Article 200 where fraudulent VAT refund is proven. Penalties include retrospective denial of the 0% rate, imposition of the 10% standard VAT on the full gross consideration, interest at 20% per annum, fines ranging from 1 to 3 times the under-declared tax for evasion and up to VND 100,000,000 for administrative violations, and clawback of all refunded input VAT, in addition to suspended or revoked tax identification/customs registration codes in severe cases.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: State Bank of Vietnam (SBV; Vietnamese: Ngan Hang Nha Nuoc Viet Nam), acting principally through the Foreign Exchange Management Department and the municipal/provincial SBV branches that license, supervise, and receive regulatory filings from the commercial bank selected to host the Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) and the operational foreign-currency accounts of the foreign-invested limited liability company.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Viet Nam has accepted IMF Article VIII obligations and therefore maintains de jure convertibility for current-account transactions, which includes the export of remote BPO and call-center services (booking of fees, commissions, and management charges by the LLC from offshore principals). In practice, however, the convertibility regime is procedural and bank-intermediated: all foreign-currency receipts must flow through an SBV-licensed authorized credit institution; service receivables denominated in USD or EUR must be credited to an authorized foreign-currency account maintained in Viet Nam; and conversion into VND is executed at the commercial bank's counter rate, which is disciplined by the SBV's daily central rate and the prescribed trading band. Capital-account transactions remain fully controlled: equity injections, shareholder loans, and liquidation or exit proceeds are subject to mandatory registration, use of the DICA, and prior documentary verification under Circular No. 05/2021/TT-NHNN. Profit remittance is permitted as a current-account transfer but is effectively conditioned on (i) completion of the audited annual financial statements, (ii) finalization of corporate income tax and all other statutory obligations, (iii) confirmation that all matured liabilities to Vietnamese creditors have been discharged, (iv) a board resolution declaring the distribution, and (v) the commercial bank's verification that the remitted amount does not exceed the accumulated after-tax distributable profit reflected in the audited equity accounts. For this BPO LLC, the material operational hurdle is not legal convertibility but the documentary discipline required for each USD receipt and each VND conversion, and the absolute prohibition against settling service export fees outside the licensed banking channel.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For service exports (remote BPO and call-center activities), the statutory rule is full repatriation rather than surrender: 100% of the foreign-currency proceeds earned from services rendered to offshore clients must be credited to a foreign-currency or VND account held with an SBV-licensed authorized bank in Viet Nam. The applicable repatriation period is 180 days from the date the service is performed or, where the underlying client contract establishes payment milestones, 180 days from each invoice due date; the LLC must monitor each receivable against this deadline and in no case may it retain service proceeds offshore. There is currently no mandatory conversion ratio or export surrender quota applicable to service exporters of this type: the LLC may lawfully retain the full 100% of collected USD in its foreign-currency operating account or convert all or part to VND at the licensed bank. Nevertheless, the SBV retains discretionary authority, in exceptional balance-of-payments stress scenarios, to impose temporary conversion obligations by legal instrument, and the licensed bank is obligated to notify the SBV of any overdue or unrepatriated service receipt, which may trigger administrative sanctions, adverse BoP status, and heightened scrutiny at the next annual account review.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.capital_and_profit_remittance_procedural: The LLC must open a Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at a licensed commercial bank under Circular No. 05/2021/TT-NHNN. All paid-in capital and shareholder loans enter exclusively through the DICA, and all outbound repatriations of capital, loan principal, and dividends exit exclusively through the DICA. Service-export receipts and ordinary operating receipts must be segregated into current-account foreign-currency accounts so that the bank can certify the DICA balance with confidence. A profit remittance requires submission of the audited financial statements for the year in which the profit arose, the corporate income tax finalization receipt, confirmation of full settlement of payables, the shareholders' resolution on dividend distribution, and a written remittance instruction identifying the exact USD amount; the remitting bank verifies compliance, obtains the LLC's confirmation, and files the transaction with the SBV under the balance-of-payments reporting regime.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low, with a constrained secondary role. Offshore digital EMIs and cross-border payment platforms (Wise B2B, Revolut Business, Airwallex, Payoneer, and similar) cannot hold SBV-regulated VND accounts, cannot provide onshore clearing, and cannot serve as the legal settlement rail for Vietnamese balance-of-payments reporting. VND is not internationally deliverable, and any EMI custody of BPO service receivables creates shadow-accounting risk, non-compliance with the 180-day repatriation rule, and a break in the audit trail required by Circular No. 05/2021/TT-NHNN. The only viable architecture is a collection-rail model: Wise or an equivalent EMI may be used for low-ticket inbound fees collected from offshore end clients, provided that (i) the EMI account is established in the exact name of the Vietnamese LLC or its authorized treasury nominee, (ii) a daily or weekly sweep by SWIFT MT103 transfers the cleared proceeds into the LLC's foreign-currency account at the licensed Vietnamese bank, and (iii) the LLC's books, the BoP filings, and the audited financial statements recognize the principal only at the Vietnamese licensed bank. High-ticket strategic receivables from the BPO principals should be wired directly via SWIFT MT103 to the licensed Vietnamese bank. Feasibility rating: Low for primary treasury and clearing functionality; Medium only as a secondary aggregation point for marginal retail-scale collections.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is mandatory in substance. For the initial account opening of a foreign-invested LLC, the legal representative (Chairman or General Director), any authorized signatories, and the natural-person beneficial owners (typically holders of 10% or more of charter capital or persons exercising effective control) must appear in person at the chosen bank's treasury or corporate branch in Hanoi or Ho Chi Minh City to present original passports and complete the on-premises identification and interview process. Remote video-KYC and digital-only onboarding are not accepted as a lawful substitute for the first account mandate of this structure. Where a foreign director is not resident in Viet Nam, the LLC must appoint a local resident legal representative and grant a power of attorney; the POA must be notarized in the home jurisdiction and either apostilled (Hague Convention, as applicable) or consular-legalized, must be translated into Vietnamese by a licensed translation office, and must still be accompanied by at least one in-person banking compliance meeting held in Viet Nam. After the initial onboarding, ongoing operations, including subsequent signatory additions and FX mandate amendments, may be executed through bank-approved e-banking token procedures without repeated physical attendance.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: low registered charter capital relative to projected high-volume USD service-export turnover, creating a mismatch that suggests unregistered capital inflow or undeclared foreign ownership.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit the Investment Registration Certificate and Enterprise Registration Certificate showing the charter capital and capital contribution schedule; the bank's DICA credit advices evidencing each tranche of paid-in capital; the LLC's board resolution on capital utilization; a 12-month treasury forecast reconciling the small capital base with recurring BPO fee revenue; written service contracts with the offshore principals; and the audited opening balance sheet demonstrating that operating expenses are funded from service revenue rather than shareholder loans.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: heavy use of Wise or another offshore EMI in the receipts trail, which the bank may profile as an unauthorized money remitter or an attempt to circumvent BoP reporting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide a formal treasury policy naming the licensed Vietnamese bank as the exclusive settlement institution; the LLC's client-mandate letters instructing each offshore principal to remit contract fees by SWIFT MT103 directly to the Vietnamese bank account; the EMI account-opening confirmation and UBO declaration; MT103 sweep receipts from the EMI to the Vietnamese operating account; and a reconciliation ledger showing that every EMI receipt is booked only upon credit at the licensed bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: telemarketing and remote call-center scope included in NAICS/ISIC mapping triggers consumer-protection typologies, including money mule recruitment, financial-products cold calling, or card-not-present fraud exposure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the complete client-contract inventory describing the call types (inbound helpdesk and outbound tele-sales campaigns), a compliance and call-script QA policy, a ban on soliciting payment details over the phone, evidence of campaign-level approvals by principals, a sample outbound campaign targeting list with suppression procedures, the complaints and data-subject-request log, and confirmation of adherence to Viet Nam's personal data protection regime under Decree No. 13/2023/ND-CP.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: outbound disbursements to foreign suppliers, freelancer settlement agents, or mixed payroll jurisdictions in offshore or high-risk locations, which may suggest conversion of the LLC into an unlicensed remitter.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the approved vendor list with registered addresses and tax identifications; underlying invoices for marketing, software, cloud telephony, and subcontract services; the payroll register and social insurance filings proving that Vietnamese employees are paid exclusively through the licensed bank in VND; and a written treasury undertaking that no employee wages are settled through cryptocurrency, cash, or third-country aggregators.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: foreign signatories with no Vietnamese tax identification, no local residential registration, and no verifiable business address.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the LLC's lease agreement for the Vietnamese service delivery center, evidence of the locally resident legal representative with valid work permit or temporary residence card, the Vietnamese tax identification code of the LLC, the apostilled power of attorney granted to the local representative, original board resolutions identifying all authorized signatories, and signed specimen signatures certified at the bank's premises.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: All inbound equity capital must be routed by SWIFT MT103 from the foreign shareholder's bank account directly to the LLC's Direct Investment Capital Account (DICA) at the licensed Vietnamese commercial bank. The remittance instruction must identify the LLC by its Enterprise Registration Code and Investment Registration Certificate number and must state a purpose code corresponding to direct-investment equity contribution; the bank will credit the funds, register the inflow in the DICA ledger, and report the transaction to the State Bank of Vietnam under the balance-of-payments framework. The LLC may then effect a spot conversion of the USD capital to VND and transfer the VND to its payroll/operating account. Service-export fees from offshore BPO principals must not be commingled with the DICA; they are current-account receipts and must be received into a separate foreign-currency operating account. Where the principals are invoiced monthly, the LLC should include the invoice number and the BPO contract reference in each incoming MT103 so that the bank can map the receipt to the underlying service export and verify compliance with the 180-day repatriation rule.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Local disbursements, including employee salaries, social insurance, rent, and Vietnamese vendor payments, are executed in VND through the local interbank clearing system managed by the National Payment Corporation of Viet Nam (NAPAS), using the licensed bank's e-banking platform. Cross-border outbound disbursements, including license fees for cloud telephony and CRM software, foreign supplier payments, and tax advisory retainers, are cleared via SWIFT MT103 direct transfers or, where a correspondent intermediary is required, MT103 plus MT202 cover. Dividends and capital repatriation must be cleared outbound through the DICA via SWIFT MT103, supported by the audited financial statements, the CIT finalization certificate, the board resolution, and the bank's verification that the remittance does not exceed distributable after-tax profit. Commercial letters of credit are not a standard or necessary rail for an ISIC 7820 remote BPO/call-center operation because the underlying transactions are service fees rather than physical commodity shipments; high-value equipment purchases may be settled by documentary collection or MT103 against the supply agreement, reserving the LC structure only if the LLC later acquires physical hardware on a cross-border deferred-payment basis.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright VND/USD FX forward contracts entered into with an SBV-licensed authorized bank, permitted only where the LLC demonstrates a genuine underlying foreign-currency exposure arising from service export receivables, payroll conversion requirements, or registered shareholder loans; speculative or non-deliverable offshore-linked forward structures are prohibited.

VND/USD FX swap transactions (both odd-leg and straight-swap structures) with an SBV-licensed authorized bank, used to manage the timing mismatch between USD service-receipt conversion and periodic VND payroll and rental payment obligations.

Cross-currency swaps executed between the LLC and a licensed bank or between the LLC and its foreign shareholder, provided the underlying shareholder loan or intercompany payable has been duly registered with the State Bank of Vietnam and the swap terminates on or before the maturity of the recognized underlying exposure.

FX option structures (call or put options on VND) purchased from an SBV-licensed authorized bank, subject to the same genuine-demand rule requiring the notional to fall within the forecast USD service receipts and committed VND expenditure over the option tenor.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs): not permitted as an onshore instrument for a Vietnamese resident entity; the LLC may not novate offshore NDF contracts into VND delivery, may not use offshore NDF desks without prior SBV authorization, and must rely exclusively on deliverable onshore forwards and swaps for lawful hedges.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Business License Tax (Lệ phí môn bài) declaration and payment
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 30 January each tax year for existing enterprises
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03%/day on unpaid tax; administrative fines up to VND 100 million under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; continued non-payment may trigger tax enforcement and business registration consequences

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Corporate Income Tax (CIT) finalisation return for prior fiscal year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March immediately following the tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-payment interest at 0.03%/day on underpaid CIT; late-filing penalties up to VND 100 million under Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; severe or repeated violations may lead to forced collection and operational suspension

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Tax Department and Department of Planning and Investment / Business Registration Office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after fiscal year-end (typically by 31 March)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines for late submission ranging from VND 2–20 million (Decree 41/2018, amended by Decree 177/2020); failure to audit when compulsory may attract fines up to VND 50 million and heightened tax audit risk

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Foreign Investment Project Implementation Report
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Provincial Department of Planning and Investment / Investment Registration Authority
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually as specified on the Investment Registration Certificate; standard compliance window is by 31 March following the reporting year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative penalties for late or non-filing under Decree 122/2021/ND-CP (typically VND 10–15 million); repeated breaches may be recorded against the investment project and affect future approvals or incentive eligibility

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: All foreign-invested limited liability companies in Vietnam are compulsorily subject to annual independent audit regardless of size; domestic private enterprises are audited only if they meet thresholds under Decree 17/2012/ND-CP or are listed/public-interest entities
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Vietnam Accounting Standards (VAS) under Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC; IFRS permitted for consolidated financial reporting only under Circular 99/2021/TT-BTC

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Vietnam does not maintain a public UBO register. The LLC must maintain an accurate member register and update it within 10 days of any capital stake transfer, pledge or change. The annual Foreign Investment Project Report and IRC modification procedure serve as the de facto annual ownership confirmation for foreign investors; a control person statement is typically included in the audited financial statements and corporate minutes.

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: High-tech enterprises, software production, and certain qualifying activities may benefit from a 10% preferential CIT rate for 15 years plus a 4-year CIT exemption and 9-year 50% reduction. Small and medium enterprises may temporarily use a 15-20% rate in specific transitional windows. No blanket offshore BPO call-center incentive applies unless the entity holds an eligible high-tech or software certificate.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 02/TNDN (Annual Finalization Return) submitted via the Vietnam e-Tax Portal (https://etaxvn.gdt.gov.vn) integrated with the General Department of Taxation (GDT) electronic filing system; provisional quarterly payments use Form 01/TNDN or the quarterly declaration in the same portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual finalization with quarterly provisional CIT payments
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Quarterly provisional CIT payments due no later than the 30th day after the end of each quarter; the annual finalization return is due no later than the last day of the 3rd month from the end of the fiscal year (typically 31 March for a calendar-year taxpayer, or the last day of month 3 after the fiscal year ends for approved fiscal years).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax code, taxpayer name, fiscal year, tax administration office, and declaration page indicators.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-invested LLC must input its enterprise tax code (mã số thuế) and registered head-office address; indicate quarterly declaration codes attached if provisional returns were filed.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total assessable revenue derived from business activities including BPO service fees, inbound helpdesk subscription fees, and outbound tele-sales commissions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include only Vietnam-sourced revenue allocable to the permanent establishment; clarify revenue recognition per Circular 200/2014/TT-BTC if cross-border service revenue is partly sourced from offshore clients.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating costs, salaries, telecom infrastructure, software, rent, depreciation, and administrative expenses satisfying the actual-nexus and invoicing conditions under Circular 96/2015/TT-BTC.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident managers must ensure invoices and expense proof are retained in Vietnam; payments to overseas affiliates require TP documentation and may be disallowed if no substance or if not at arm's length.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Expenses that exceed statutory caps, non-compliant invoices, provisions without statutory basis, and fines or penalties not permitted under CIT law.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: List intercompany management fees that fail the substance or benchmark test, non-registered payments, and any costs lacking valid e-invoices or vouchers.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Prior-year tax losses carried forward up to 5 consecutive years from the year of loss, as verified by the tax authority during finalization.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign investors must attach loss-carryforward schedules and supporting finalization decisions; losses of a foreign parent cannot be set off against the Vietnam LLC's taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income before incentives; including adjustments for non-deductible items and other statutory add-backs or deductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Submit the computation with clear reconciliation of accounting profit to taxable income; if claiming a high-tech/software incentive, attach the certificate and incentive schedule.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box C1 (CIT payable at headline rate)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax payable computed at the 20% statutory rate applied to taxable income.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders must nevertheless ensure the entity applies the correct rate and does not unilaterally apply an offshore effective rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deduction or reduction of CIT for preferential rates, exemptions, and tax holidays.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only claim incentives after obtaining a written confirmation or approved tax incentive schedule from the local tax authority; attach applicable certificates.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Credits for foreign taxes paid on foreign-source income included in Vietnam taxable income, where an applicable DTA or unilateral credit rule applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Include certified foreign tax credit evidence (tax assessment or TRC from the source country).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box D (Final CIT due and prior payments reconciliation)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final CIT due after provisional payments, incentives, and credits; amount payable or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The LLC must remit the balance within the statutory deadline; any offset of overpaid provisional tax requires a formal reconciliation to the GDT.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the annual finalization return incurs a fine up to VND 15,000,000 to 35,000,000 depending on delay, plus a late-payment interest charge of 0.03% per day on the unpaid tax amount. Failure to submit attached transfer-pricing and e-invoice datasets may trigger additional fines for violations of tax administration procedures under Law No. 38/2019/QH14.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 0% on dividends paid by a Vietnamese LLC to its corporate shareholder if the shareholder is a foreign juridical person under common application of the Law on Enterprise and the CIT Law, provided the LLC's after-tax profit is lawfully distributed; however, a 0.1% registration fee on equity transfers is not a dividend WHT. Dividends to foreign individuals are subject to a 5% personal income tax where applicable, but for corporate shareholders using a Vietnam LLC, the dividend itself is not subject to additional CIT. Where the foreign shareholder is a country without a DTA, domestic rules still do not impose a dividend WHT at the LLC level; instead cross-border payments (interest, royalties, services) require a contractor tax exposure.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke DTA relief, the foreign parent must (i) obtain a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) from the competent authority of the residence jurisdiction, (ii) submit a completed DTA relief application form and TRC to the Vietnamese withholding agent or GDT, (iii) obtain a Vietnamese tax identification number for the foreign party if required by local administrative procedures, and (iv) where the payment is a dividend, interest, or royalty, file the standard application for application of the DTA before the transaction or at the latest before the withholding tax is finalized; the GDT may require the TRC to be legalized or notarized translated into Vietnamese depending on the treaty's administrative arrangement. For reduced rates, the beneficial ownership condition must be satisfied; conduit applicants without substance will be denied treaty benefits.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: interest WHT for offshore lenders is 5% (deemed CIT) plus no VAT, and royalties or franchise/IP service fees are subject to a combined Foreign Contractor Tax (FCT) regime: 10% VAT on the gross payment plus CIT at 10% for royalty income, or services at 5% CIT; overall effective tax burden for royalties is 20% (10% CIT + 10% VAT). Under Vietnam's DTAs, interest is commonly reduced to 10% (e.g., with many OECD treaty partners, sometimes lower per specific treaty), while royalties are commonly reduced to 10% or 5% depending on the treaty and IP type; a 10% VAT cannot be treaty-reduced, as VAT is a domestic indirect tax.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Local File and Master File thresholds apply to a related-party transaction taxpayer where total related-party revenue exceeds VND 50 billion (approximately USD 2 million) or where the transaction value exceeds VND 30 billion, under Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and Circular 105/2021/TT-BTC. Even if below thresholds, a taxpayer must prepare a TP dossier by 30 November for the previous fiscal year if it engages in controlled transactions; smaller taxpayers may complete the TP declaration form instead. In practice, all foreign-invested BPO entities must maintain contemporaneous TP documentation to protect against adjustment risk.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vietnam does not maintain a codified 'Economic Substance Regulations' such as the UAE regime, but the General Anti-Avoidance Rule (GAAR) under Article 26 of Decree 132/2020/ND-CP and the substance-over-form principle in tax administration allow recharacterization of transactions lacking business purpose. A foreign-owned BPO call center must demonstrate substantive personnel in Vietnam, active decision-making, contractual risk assumption, and actual operational control over telecommunication and CRM systems; failure to evidence substance for intercompany service charges may lead to full disallowance of the cost, especially for fees routed to tax havens.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Willful omission of BPO service revenue, issuance of fake e-invoices for non-existent call-center services to inflate deductions, underreporting foreign-source revenue, or false beneficiary declarations to obtain DTA reduced rates.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to 1 to 3 times the evaded tax amount under Law No. 38/2019/QH14 and Decree 125/2020/ND-CP; criminal prosecution under the Penal Code for tax evasion involving amounts over VND 100 million yields fines up to VND 4.5 billion and imprisonment up to 3-7 years for organized or large-scale evasion, plus an obligation to pay the full underpaid tax and interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Legal representatives, financial directors, and authorized signatories risk criminal liability if they knew or ordered the misdeclaration; the court can impose a cumulative sentence, travel bans, freezing of personal assets, and restitution orders; tax administration may issue a coercive collection order against the director's personal bank accounts if the company is dissolved or asset-emptied.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating the BPO LLC with zero or minimal staff, no physical office, no payroll records, using the entity solely as a pass-through to funnel profits to a related offshore entity, or artificially splitting contracts to stay below the TP document threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Recharacterization of the entity's income to the true economic owner; disallowance of all intercompany deductions; application of a deemed profit determination under Decree 132/2020; penalties for false tax declaration up to 3 times the tax shortfall and additional late-payment interest.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Director may be jointly liable for the corporate tax debt when the corporate veil is pierced under Vietnamese law due to fraud or abusive use of a legal entity; civil damages to tax authorities and creditors; travel restrictions and mandatory appearance orders can be issued to prevent flight.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Pricing BPO services (per-seat fees, per-minute charges, helpdesk fees) to the foreign parent below market margin, accumulating persistent losses over 5 years while paying overseas service fees, or failing to prepare a Local File and Master File for controlled transactions above the VND 50 billion threshold.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment by GDT with additional CIT at 20% plus late-payment interest at 0.03% per day; administrative penalty equal to 20% of the underpaid tax where the mispricing is not fraud, and up to 3 times for fraudulent concealment; compulsory filing of TP documentation with adjusted returns.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false TP documentation or authorize circular transactions may be subject to criminal tax evasion provisions; personal assets can be attached through enforcement procedures for the company's unpaid tax; foreign directors can be subject to entry bans or denial of exit visas pending settlement.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Using the Wise B2B or wire transfer accounts to split credits into sub-threshold remittances, invoicing a nominee/pass-through entity to obscure beneficial ownership, or handling converted funds from clients that originate in sanctioned jurisdictions without performing KYC/CDD.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering Law (effective 2023), failure to report unusual transactions results in fines up to VND 200 million and suspension of business activities for serious violations; banks must freeze accounts; criminal money-laundering charges attract imprisonment up to 10 years plus fines up to VND 100 million for individuals, and VND 3 billion for organizations.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners of the Vietnamese LLC may be criminally prosecuted for facilitating money laundering if they knowingly process illicit proceeds; personal travel bans, asset forfeiture, and Social Insurance or tax clearance refusal may block departure; the State Bank of Vietnam can blacklist controllers from maintaining payment-service relationships.
